learningObjective: Explain what AOTAutograd captures beyond the forward graph and how the joint (forward+backward) graph is used.

canonicalClaims.claim: AOTAutograd traces a joint forward+backward FX graph, then partitions it into forward and backward subgraphs (with a recompute/save decision) that are compiled by Inductor; this enables a compiled backward pass under torch.compile.
conditions: Autograd is active for the compiled call.
nonImplications: Does not imply the compiled backward is always faster than eager backward.
Does not imply the partitioner always makes optimal save/recompute choices.

misconceptions.whyWrong: It traces a joint fw+bw graph.
It is a tracer + graph partitioner; not a device placement scheduler.
It operates on the traced FX graph, not on Python source.

misconceptions.claim: AOTAutograd forces all backward ops to run eagerly.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The backward is compiled together with the forward when possible.

implementationFacts: The joint graph is captured via a functional-tracing approach
The partitioner decides which activations to save vs. recompute
Backward subgraph is compiled through Inductor like the forward
performanceScenarios: Compiled backward reduces per-op dispatch cost; save-vs-recompute choices trade memory for compute.
